subject.title: feat(self-host): local console sign-in without Cloudflare Access

question: Should self-host upgrades enable local console authentication by default, or should existing API-only deployments require an explicit CLAWROUTER_LOCAL_AUTH=enabled opt-in?
rationale: Both modes are implemented, but the choice changes the externally reachable self-host console surface for existing deployments and cannot be resolved from code correctness alone.

options.title: Keep existing posture by default
options.body: Default local auth to disabled and require an explicit enabled setting so v0.1.0 upgrades retain the API-only console boundary.

options.title: Adopt default-on local sign-in
options.body: Keep enabled as the default and explicitly accept that self-host upgrades expose the sign-in shell and endpoint while APIs remain session-gated.

recommendation.title: Keep existing posture by default
recommendation.body: Default local auth to disabled and require an explicit enabled setting so v0.1.0 upgrades retain the API-only console boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged self-host profile whose documented v1 limitation and upgrade contract this PR changes.
